headline: ReproBridge reports higher AI reproduction success from reusable experiment artifacts
summary: A preprint published on 2026-11-05 introduces ReproBridge, a workflow that packages refined research code, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide for reuse by later coding agents. The authors evaluate it on 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 selected ICML 2026 Spotlight papers. Across four tested coding-agent models, they report mean task reproduction success rising from 76.4% with raw code to 92.6% with refined artifacts and downstream API spending falling by 19.7% on average. Five human-verified reference measurements per task and execution-evidence audits are part of the reported protocol. These results are author-reported; code and dataset were not publicly linked on the inspected project page, and the study does not establish scientific validity, conference-wide reproduction rates, or benefits to human researchers.
